neet_phy_u13_t12_1.working: Diamagnetic susceptibility arises from induced orbital moments, not from thermal alignment of permanent dipoles. So it is essentially independent of temperature. Paramagnetic and ferromagnetic susceptibilities both depend on temperature.

neet_phy_u13_t12_2.working: By Curie's law, χ ∝ 1/T. So χ = 3.0e-4 × 300/200 = 4.5e-4.

neet_phy_u13_t12_3.working: By the Curie-Weiss law, χ = C/(T − Tc). At 731 K, T − Tc = 100 K. Halving χ requires T − Tc = 200 K, so T = 831 K.

neet_phy_u13_t12_4.working: Above Tc, ferromagnets become paramagnetic, so A is true. Their susceptibility follows χ = C/(T − Tc) and still depends on temperature, so R is false.

neet_phy_u13_t12_5.working: Gadolinium has Tc ≈ 293 K, so at 330 K it is paramagnetic. Nickel has Tc = 631 K, so at 330 K it is ferromagnetic. Statement I is false. In a weak field M = C·B/T, so doubling both B and T leaves M unchanged. Statement II is true.
